findings.claim: The oxygen debt is repaid after exercise as lactic acid is oxidised to CO2 and water in the liver.
findings.truth: The lesson says twice elsewhere (collapsible n13, key fact n21, takeaway n26) that the liver converts lactic acid back to glucose. That is the standard GCSE account (Cori cycle). Oxidation of lactate happens mainly in muscle and heart, not the liver, so the sentence both contradicts the lesson and misplaces the process.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with n13/n21/n26; settled physiology (liver gluconeogenesis). J260 B4.1 does not cover oxygen debt, so the lesson's own account is the only authority.

findings.field: content_html, conclusion_html, exam_tip_html, practice_questions, knowledge_checks, flashcard_questions
findings.claim: DNA replication occurs during S phase, before mitosis begins ... state clearly that DNA replication happens before mitosis, in S phase.
findings.truth: Correct science, wrong vocabulary for this board. B4.3.1a is 'describe the role of the cell cycle in growth, including interphase and mitosis', with the note 'Learners are not expected to recall intermediate phases'. The lesson names S phase seven times and never uses the word interphase, so a student meeting 'interphase' in the paper has never seen it.
findings.evidence: spec B4.3.1a and its 'intermediate phases' note (specs/ocr/combined-science-b-21c-J260.md line ~3379).

findings.claim: Red blood cells are biconcave discs with no nucleus - this removes the nucleus and increases the surface area for oxygen-carrying haemoglobin.
findings.truth: Circular ('no nucleus ... this removes the nucleus') and it attaches the wrong reason to each adaptation. The biconcave shape increases surface area for oxygen uptake; the absent nucleus leaves more room for haemoglobin. The lesson's own mark scheme and flashcard state it correctly.
findings.evidence: settled fact; internal contradiction with practice_questions[1] and flashcard[4].

findings.claim: As the cube grows, its surface area-to-volume ratio halves and then halves again.
findings.truth: The three figures given in the same paragraph are 6:1, 3:1 and 2:1. Recomputed: 1 cm cube 6/1 = 6:1; 2 cm cube 24/8 = 3:1; 3 cm cube 54/27 = 2:1. The first step halves, the second does not (3 to 2). The stated pattern contradicts the numbers immediately before it.

findings.claim: use all four design features: large surface area, thin wall, steep concentration gradient, and moisture (for gas exchange). Missing one feature typically loses a mark.
findings.truth: The lesson's own 2-mark scheme awards 'Large surface area; thin walls; good blood supply (two of three for 2 marks)' and the key fact lists three features. B5.1.7 asks learners to explain the need for exchange surfaces in terms of surface area:volume ratio; moisture is not a required feature for this board. Telling students they lose a mark for omitting it is wrong.
findings.evidence: spec B5.1.7; internal contradiction with practice_questions[1].marks and key fact n20.

findings.claim: Glucagon content sits inside a correct higher-only wrapper in content_html (n7), but leaks unflagged into the conclusion takeaway, one practice question, two knowledge checks and two flashcards.
findings.truth: B5.6.2 ('explain how glucagon and insulin work together to control the blood sugar level') is bold in the spec, so Higher tier only; the narrative bold is 'and glucagon acting antagonistically'. B5.6.1 (insulin alone) is both tiers. The wrapper on n7 is correct and stays. Foundation students cannot see n7, so the unflagged items are unanswerable for them.

findings.claim: The four-hormone menstrual chain and IVF are correctly wrapped as higher-only (n3, n7, n8), but the n4 key fact repeats the whole chain outside the wrapper, and both conclusion takeaways, four practice questions, four knowledge checks and seven flashcards test the hidden content without a tier flag.
findings.truth: B5.5.2 ('explain the interactions of FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone') and B5.5.4 ('explain the use of hormones in modern reproductive technologies to treat infertility') are both bold, as is the whole seven-bullet hormone narrative. B5.5.1 (hormones control the menstrual cycle, including ovulation) and B5.5.3 (contraception) stay at both tiers. Preferred remedy for the n4 key fact would be a real <div class="higher-only"> wrapper, but that also needs narration_manifest entry n4 flagged tier:"higher" (n3/n7/n8 already are), which _edits.json cannot express - so the fix labels the Higher part inline instead, keeping the Foundation-safe sentence first.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/combined-science-b-21c-J260-bold.md B5.5 (bold narrative bullets, bold outcomes 2 and 4); narration_manifest tiers read from _raw.json.

findings.claim: Unit named 'biology-paper-2' although J260 has one biology paper (Biology /01, 95 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 26.4%; Paper 4 /04 assesses all content, 75 marks, 20.8%; Higher mirrors as Papers 5-8).
findings.truth: Lesson-to-chapter mapping checked and sound: L1 -> B4.1; L2 -> B4.2; L3 -> B4.3 + B4.4; L4 -> B5.1; L5 -> B5.2 + B5.3; L6 -> B5.4 + B5.6; L7 -> B5.5 + B5.6; L8 -> B6.1 + B6.2 + B6.3. The split is Gateway-shaped naming only. No lesson claims a paper number, duration, mark total, tier structure or 'Paper 2 covers' anywhere in the unit; no Gateway codes, no 'required practicals' or 'core practicals' wording, no AQA/Edexcel wording, no banned mark-scheme phrases. Nothing to edit; the unit slug is a naming decision for Tom.
findings.evidence: spec assessment overview (Paper 1 assesses B1-B6 and BCP7/8; J260/01 95 marks 1 h 45 min 26.4%); full-text scan of the eight lessons.

findings.claim: Both-tier B4-B6 assessable outcomes that no lesson in the unit teaches.
findings.truth: Missing: B4.3.2 cancer as uncontrolled growth and division (the word 'cancer' appears nowhere); B4.3.3 meiosis and gametes (meiosis appears only as a wrong option in an L3 knowledge check; 'gamete' and 'zygote' appear nowhere); B4.3.4 meristems in plants; B5.1.4 heart structure (cardiac muscle, chambers, valves - 'atria' and 'ventricle' appear nowhere); B5.1.6 plasma adaptations ('plasma' appears nowhere); B6.1.6 selective breeding of food plants and domesticated animals; B6.1.2 genetic variants arising from mutations (only glanced at in L8 speciation). B6.1.8 antibiotic resistance appears only in an L8 mark scheme, not in the lesson body. These are teaching gaps, not errors - they need new lessons or new sections, which is Tom's call.
findings.evidence: spec B4.3, B5.1, B6.1 assessable learning outcomes; term scan across raw/L01-L08.

findings.claim: The 'Water Balance and the Kidneys' section teaches osmoregulation, ADH and pituitary control of water reabsorption, and is tested by practice question 1, one match pair and one flashcard.
findings.truth: 'ADH', 'anti-diuretic', 'osmoregulation', 'vasodilation', 'vasoconstriction', 'sweat' and 'shiver' appear nowhere in the J260 spec. The only kidney statement is in B5.1: 'Urea is filtered out of the blood by the kidneys into urine.' B5.4 asks only for the importance of a constant internal environment plus graph work, and its suggested practicals are about body temperature - so the thermoregulation section has a spec anchor but the ADH section does not. Removing it would delete narration block n14, which the edit format forbids. Options: (a) leave as enrichment but replace the ADH practice question, match pair and flashcard with in-spec items; (b) reword n14 to the B5.1 urea statement and re-narrate; (c) leave untouched.
findings.evidence: spec B5.4 outcomes and practical work; grep of the whole spec for ADH / osmoregulation / vasodilation returns nothing.

findings.claim: The second half of L7 teaches kidney failure, dialysis, kidney transplant, immunosuppressants and other organ replacement, tested by two practice questions, one knowledge check and four flashcards.
findings.truth: J260 B5.6 has only three outcomes, all about insulin, glucagon and comparing type 1 and type 2 diabetes. 'Dialysis' appears in the spec only as dialysis tubing in a B3.1 diffusion practical; 'transplant', 'immunosuppressant' and 'donor' appear nowhere. The science taught is correct, but it is not examinable content for this qualification. Same options as F10: replace the assessment items, reword the narration blocks (n10-n14), or leave as enrichment.
findings.evidence: spec B5.6 assessable learning outcomes; grep of the whole spec for dialysis / transplant / immunosuppressant.

findings.claim: Reflex arcs bypass the brain - the signal goes through the spinal cord only ... Other reflexes include the pupil reflex.
findings.truth: The pupil light reflex is processed in the brainstem, not the spinal cord, so the absolute 'spinal cord only' sits oddly next to the example. The spec's own wording is 'without involving a processing centre', which mark schemes accept, so no edit is proposed.

findings.claim: The osmosis dfn and glossary entry define osmosis using 'high water potential' and 'low water potential'.
findings.truth: B3.1.2 carries the note 'Learners are not expected to explain osmosis in terms of water potential'. The body text (n7) correctly uses dilute/concentrated, so the parentheticals are extra rather than wrong.

findings.claim: Flashcard 12 asks 'What drives the transpiration stream in plants?'
findings.truth: Correct answer, but the lesson never mentions transpiration, xylem or stomata; that content sits in B3.1, not B5.1. The card tests something this lesson does not teach.

findings.claim: His observations of finch beak shapes on the Galapagos Islands - each suited to a different food source - helped him form the idea that species change.
findings.truth: A standard textbook simplification. Darwin did not sort the finches by island during the voyage; John Gould's 1837 analysis of the specimens was the turning point. Not worth an edit at GCSE, but it is not history as written.

findings.claim: Induced pluripotent stem cells are taught in a collapsible, a knowledge check and two flashcards.
findings.truth: B4.4 has one outcome: discuss potential benefits, risks and ethical issues of stem cells in medicine. iPS cells are not named in the spec, but they are a legitimate vehicle for that ethical discussion, so this is enrichment rather than an error.

summary: Eight lessons checked against J260 (chapters B4-B6). Seven FIX findings, 35 edits: one physiology contradiction (L1 lactic acid), one off-spec phase name taught as the required answer (L3 interphase), one garbled red blood cell adaptation (L3), one arithmetic claim that contradicts its own figures (L4 SA:V), one exam-technique claim that contradicts the lesson's own mark scheme (L4 moisture), and two tier leaks where correct higher-only wrappers are undermined by unflagged summaries and assessment items (L6 glucagon, L7 menstrual cycle and IVF). Four ADJUDICATE items: the lesson-to-chapter mapping (sound, naming only), seven both-tier B4-B6 outcomes taught nowhere, and two blocks of correct but off-spec content (L6 ADH/osmoregulation, L7 dialysis/transplant). No wrong paper claims, no Gateway wording, no banned mark-scheme phrases, no placeholder questions, no answer-key errors: all 40 knowledge checks and every worked calculation recomputed clean.
